findings.claim: WARMUP is now 65, which contradicts the read-only protocol draft's 'WARMUP = 60 literal ... every harness window starts 60 sessions before the period start' (E5_CEILING_protocol_draft.json family.features_ranked.warmup); nothing in the repo reads the literal yet (idxsig/e5.py does not exist; e3.py/e4.py and backtest.run have no lead-in logic, backtest.run slices the panel to [start, end] and computes signals on that slice), so the deviation is harmless today but must be reconciled when research/E5/protocol.json is frozen and e5.py is written.
findings.evidence: python3 -I json walk of the draft prints '.family.features_ranked.warmup : WARMUP = 60 literal: compute() returns NaN for the first 60 sessions of its view; every harness window starts 60 sessions before the period start'. grep -rn WARMUP idxsig/ outside moonshot_e5.py: no hits. The builder's reasoning is sound: with a 60-session lead-in the first five period sessions could never carry a flag because debounce needs five KNOWN (post-feature-warm-up) sessions behind it; my probe confirms flags are False before column 65 and identical on the common range for slices starting at 0/10/20/33.
findings.fix: No change to this file. The e5.py owner reads moonshot_e5.WARMUP (65) for the lead-in, and the protocol freeze states FEATURE_WARMUP = 60 (features) and WARMUP = 65 (compute lead-in). Already listed by the builder under needs_other_file.

findings.claim: known = isfinite(score) treats a name's sessions before its listing (and present-but-untraded sessions) as KNOWN out-of-set, because every FEATURE_ORDER column is finite from column 60 on (NaN ranks fill 0.5, binaries 0), so a name can carry a flag on its very first listed/tradeable session. This is prefix-safe and window-invariant, not a look-ahead, but it is a design choice the protocol freeze should state ('>= 5 sessions outside the top 0.5%' is satisfied vacuously by unlisted sessions).
findings.evidence: Probe on open_panel(30x220, seed 13, ipo={7: 90}, delist={9: 150}) with frozen_us_a(1.9): arm score for name 7 is finite on columns 60..89 before it is listed (state False there), its first flag lands at full column 92; flags on columns >= 65 are identical for slices starting at 0, 10, 20 and 33; causal_signals full_window_mismatches = 0 for every slice; no flags for name 9 after its delisting (tradeable mask).
findings.fix: Optional, not required for acceptance: if the protocol wants only listed sessions to count, pass known = isfinite(score) & present (or & tradeable) in flags()/family_flags(); the existing tests would still pass. Otherwise state the vacuous-history rule in the protocol text.
